title: Sharing & Collaboration System
overview: Add social features to Chisos: friend-based sharing of vinyl libraries (view-only) and collaborative meal calendars (multi-editor). This is the foundational architecture for a broader sharing journey.
goals: Enable users to share their vinyl collection with friends (view-only)
Enable collaborative meal calendars where multiple users can add meals
Build a friend system for managing trusted connections
Maintain backward compatibility with all existing single-user flows

design_decisions.rationale: Simpler model for a personal productivity app; matches the social graph users already have
One owner per resource, invited collaborators get view or edit permissions. Clear ownership semantics.
Storage layer stays dumb (user_id-scoped queries). Permission logic is explicit in routes via resolve_target_user helper.
Enables deep-linking to shared content, works with browser history, no global state needed

design_decisions.decision: Quota charges the actor (not the resource owner)
design_decisions.rationale: Prevents abuse where a user shares their calendar to get free API calls from others' quotas
Sharing is a permission layer on top of existing isolation. No migration of existing data needed.

user_profiles.description: User profiles with display name, bio, and discoverability settings
endpoints: GET /api/profile - Own profile (auto-creates from Clerk JWT if missing)
GET /api/users/<user_id>/profile - View another user's profile (requires relationship)

resource_sharing.description: Share vinyl libraries (view-only) and meal calendars (view/edit) with friends
endpoints: POST /api/shares - Create share invitation (must be friends)
GET /api/shares - List owned and received shares

vinyl_sharing.description: View-only access to a friend's vinyl collection
constraints: POST/PUT/DELETE unchanged - only owner can mutate

meal_collaboration.description: Multi-editor meal calendars where each member can add meals
modified_endpoints: POST /api/meals/transcribe?calendar_owner=<user_id> - Add meal to shared calendar
constraints: Each user can only edit/delete their own meals
Quota charges the actor, not the calendar owner
